description:
Send real reference designs from Better Design's library, so you can study how shipped products solved the same design problem before you design the user's own.

`type` picks the collection:
- `websites`: landing pages of real marketing websites, captured from the live site, sent as pictures: the hero, then the section under it. Use it before you build or redesign a landing page or a marketing section. Pass the product type and the look in `query`, such as "booking service", "creator tool", "fintech" or "minimal dark", and optionally `industry`, `style` or `theme` to filter. Name one section in `query`, such as "footer", and a site that holds a crop of that section sends the crop, at desktop width and then at phone width.
- `app-screens`: product screens of shipped apps, each rebuilt as code. Pass the product type and the screen in `query`, such as "bank home", "fitness activity summary" or "flight status", and optionally a `platform`. Apps of that product type come first, each with its best-matching flow. For an iOS or Android app, pass `platform` "mobile", "ios" or "android". iOS screens always come as SwiftUI and Android screens as React Native, on every plan and whatever `language` you pass. Pass `language` when the project is React, React Native or SwiftUI, so web screens come in that language or the nearest one the library has.
- `elements`: screens of shipped products, mostly phone apps, that show one UI element, rebuilt as code, one set per product. Pass an element type in `query`, such as "search bar", "toast" or "date picker", and optionally a `product`.
- `html-flows`: shipped flows rebuilt as HTML, so you can read their structure and copy. Pass a few words in `query`, such as "settings" or "create project". Web apps only.
- `templates`: how Better Design's finished templates are composed, such as a CRM, an inbox or a hiring tracker, as written structure with no code and no styling. Pass the screen in `query`. Use it before you build a new screen, and not when you change a screen that exists.
- `app-store-screenshots`: App Store screenshot sets, each slide rebuilt as code, with our notes on the set. Pass a `category` such as "Health & Fitness".

Use it before a redesign or a new screen, then design the user's own screen from what the references do well.

category.description: For app-store-screenshots only: an App Store category such as "Productivity". Ignores case.

context.description: Optional. One sentence on WHY you are calling this and what the user asked for (e.g. 'adding nav icons for the fintech dashboard'). Used for usage analytics, and to pick the next step a UI or UX principle answer ends with. It does not change what the tool finds.

industry.description: For websites only: keep the sites of one industry.

language.description: For app-screens, elements and app-store-screenshots: the language of the code, from what this project builds in. iOS screens always come as SwiftUI and Android screens as React Native, whatever this says. For other screens: "shopify" sends each screen as a theme section file for sections/, and "react-native" sends React, the nearest code they have. For those screens, "react", "react-native", "swiftui" and "shopify" need Pro or a trial. Defaults to "html".

limit.description: How many sets or flows to send. Defaults to 3 sets or 2 flows; at most 6 sets or 3 flows.

platform.description: For app-screens only: "ios", "android", "web", or "mobile" for iOS and Android together. A React Native or SwiftUI language searches the phone apps when this is left out.

product.description: For elements only: keep the crops of one product, such as "airbnb".

query.description: For app-screens and html-flows: words matched against flow names, such as "settings" or "invite team". For elements: the element type, such as "search bar". For websites: the product type and the look, such as "booking service" or "minimal dark", or one section, such as "footer".

style.description: For websites only: keep the sites of one visual style.

theme.description: For websites only: keep light or dark sites.

type.description: The kind of reference to send: "websites", "templates", "app-screens", "elements", "html-flows" or "app-store-screenshots".
